page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, full width. Running head at top with title and year on the left and page number on the right. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: mos[?] Scotorum arma expedientium, ex colle edito speculatus, discessum fugæ similem majori quam venisset gradu accelerat; Scoti vero milites gregarii qui ex confuso reditu trepidationem adversi agminis ex propinquo aspiciebant, Anglos hostiliter urgere vehementer cupiebant, & ægre certe à tribunis & præfectis suis contineri in suis stationibus potuerunt, qui cum ad propulsandam non inferendam injuriam arma suos induisse meminissent, extra limites innocuæ tutelæ in hoc primo belli tentamento progredien-dum non censuerunt, & confessionem hanc timoris ipsa victoria haud inferiorem judicarunt: præsertim cum ingenue postea agnoverint Angli, penes Scotos fuisse, si hostili in ipsos animo fuissent, indecorum satis reditum efficere potuisse.

Frustrata hac expeditione, non dubium erat Anglos, si qua esset ex tali discessu contracta ignominia, statim reparaturos; rumor etiam fuit eos totis viribus illud moliri; quare postridie illius diei, 5.vid. Iunii Generalis Leslius copias illas Kalsone evocat & ut sibi ad collem Dunsianum medio fere itinere occurrerent, jussit: Etenim cum satis prodidissent Angli expeditione illa in Kalsonem, propositum sibi esse Scotiam invadere, castra propius Angliam promovet Leslius, & ad collem Dunsianum (vulgo Duns Law, Dunsio municipio in Mercia propinquum; quod nativitate Iohannis Scoti Subtilis, & ludibriosa Henrici Percii Northumbriæ Comitis per pastorum crepitacula, fuga anno 1374. insigne est) sex millibus passuum ab Anglia distantem, unde prospectus esset in castra regia, posita ad alteram Tuedę ripam, loco editiori castra metatur. Ad primum Scotorum adventum Anglis prorsus inexspectatum, ad arma clamatum est in castris regiis: Nam licet antea ex profugarum Scotorum relationibus, qui apud eos commeabāt, audivissent Angli, Scotos ex adverso

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the first word of the page appears as "tnos", most likely "mos" with a damaged first letter, marked [?]. "Tuedę" is uncertain and may be "Tuedæ". The signature "A a 2" is read from a faint mark at the foot. The catchword "consistere" is read from "confistere" with the long s normalised. The page number and the year in the running head are as printed.
